newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: TEJ up more, busy on restructuring drive.
newsitem.headline: TEJ up more, busy on restructuring drive.

text.p: Shares in South African clothing firm Towles, Edgar Jacobs Ltd (TEJ) continued to rise on Wednesday as interest on its move to sell a large stake in its operations and get new controlling shareholders continued to kindle interest on the stock, dealers said.
By about 0800 GMT TEJ was up 75 cents at 825 cents, a gain of 10.0 percent with 16,800 shares having changed hands. It earlier hit a new high of 890 cents.
"It must still be this offer they've made to that Cape Town group that's pushing them high again," one Johannesburg Stock Exchange (JSE) dealer said.
"The market is seeing this move as positive news," he added.

TEJ, which is to be bought by new Western Cape-based investment group CapeStar Growth Investments, said on Monday it planned to sell its clothing operations as a going concern to subsidiary Enteeb Investments (Proprietary) Ltd.
CapeStar will hold 60 percent in Enteeb with the balance being held by management.

CapeStar consists of a consortium of investors led by former Massmart director Michael Rubin, Capital Partners and Fedsure Asset Management which paid eight million rand for 44 percent of TEJ's issued ordinary share capital, including 1.1 million previously held by the Jacobs family.
After the buy-out TEJ will be listed as CapeStar in the investments trusts sector on the JSE.
